c74object.name: evi.phaser.analog~
c74object.digest: Basic analog Phaser effect with multiple one-pole allpass stages, filtering and saturation
c74object.description:
evi.phaser.analog~ is a 'max define' for the evi_phaser_analog.gendsp gen~ abstraction. Because evi.phaser.analog~ is a 'max define' it also accepts all messages and attributes that a gen~ object does.
Analog-like phaser in the sort of pedal sense (good for mono input but still does quasi stereo well). Multple allpass filters are cascaded in series, with the amount setable via @stages. The feedback path is saturated and a crossover filter allows for selecting the frequency range of the input. The internal LFO can be shaped and skewed.

outlet.description: Internal LFO as mapped to Hz.

attribute.name: center
attribute.description: Center point around which the internal LFO modulates the frequency of the allpass filters cascade.

attribute.name: crossover
attribute.description: Crossover filter in Hz. Above this point, the Phaser effect is applied, below this point, the low end is mono and saturated. Both are summed back together on output.

attribute.name: depth
attribute.description: The size (across the frequency range) of the internal LFO modulation range.

attribute.name: duty
attribute.description: LFO: the duty cycle of the internal LFO triangle wave. Note that how much triangle wave is present in the LFO signal is dependent on the @shape attribute.

attribute.name: feedback
attribute.description: The amount of feedback added to the system, positive or negative linear gain. Along with the @pregain attribute, the feedback amount is what gives the Phaser it's character, causing notches in the output.

attribute.name: postgain
attribute.description: Gain applied to the final stage of the Allpass cascade. Effectively the output gain.

attribute.name: pregain
attribute.description: This control, along with the @feedback attribute, boosts the audio input to the cascade of allpass filters, and gives the Phaser it's character.

attribute.name: rate
attribute.description: The speed in Hz of the internal LFO. Most classic Phaser effects would keep this low and slow.

attribute.name: shape
attribute.description: LFO: interpolate between triangle (0) and sine (1) shape for the LFO. This can have a big effect on the irregularity of the Phaser movement.

attribute.name: skew
attribute.description: LFO: skew the shape of the LFO with an exponent.

attribute.name: smooth
attribute.description: This sets the lag time of all the internal smoothing of parameters in the Phaser. Parameters are smoothed by this amount in ms.

attribute.name: spread
attribute.description: The stereo spread of the effect. Internally left/right are used in a summed mono system around which spatialisation is set by this attribute. The effect therefore has a pedal-like character.

attribute.name: stages
attribute.description: This Phaser is a multistage phaser, meaning multiple allpass filters are cascaded serially to produce the effect. With this attribute you can specify how many one-pole filter stages are used. The more stages, the more absurd and 'wobbly' the effect becomes, and the stronger the effect of the @feedback. More stages use more CPU.

attribute.name: zeroreset
attribute.description: LFO: if @zeroreset is off (0, the default) the @rate attribute controls the speed (in Hz) of the internal LFOs smoothly interpolated. If on (1), the speed of the @rate attribute (and the internal phasor it controls) will only update on zero reset phase boundaries, in a 'stepped' manner but completely cleanly. This can be interesting if moving the @rate slowly, or give a random feeling if moving @rate fast.
